leading_positions.synthesis: All six members state B033 as their sole preferred prize part, with the identical trio of Drucker, Holst and Mojsov and similar citation wording (physiology of GLP-1 and its active forms enabling incretin-based therapy). All six also name the same reservations: the unresolved Mojsov versus Habener priority question, and the exclusion of Knudsen forced by the three-person cap. What is not shared is how much weight each gives to those reservations. Several members say Knudsen or the Mojsov slot should be revisited if the committee decides that drug development, rather than physiology, is the achievement. No member prefers a two-part prize in round 1, although four members raise it as an open question. No other ballot ID is in any member's preferred configuration.

areas_of_agreement: All six members place B033 alone as the preferred configuration and name the trio Drucker, Holst and Mojsov. Each argues the case on scientific merit rather than on agreement in the openings.

All six members describe the GLP-1 chain from hormone physiology to drugs as unbroken, original and mature, with large randomized outcome trials in diabetes, obesity, and cardiovascular and renal disease.

All six members list B026 (CAR-T) among their alternatives, and no member gives B026 a preferred part. Members who comment on B026 prefer a June and Sadelain core and treat Rosenberg's adoptive cell therapy and TIL work as a distinct line.
Members agree that the credit questions for B033 (Mojsov versus Habener, Knudsen) should be examined explicitly in round 2 and not assumed away.
scientific_disputes: Physiology versus drug development: members who comment prefer rewarding the discovery of mechanism (Holst, Drucker, Mojsov). Perlmann argues Knudsen would turn the prize into a drug-development award. Svenningsson says the translational step should be acknowledged and the Knudsen question recorded as a deliberate choice, and El Manira left Knudsen as a possible third slot in his opening.

B007 (optogenetics): El Manira and Svenningsson keep it as an alternative, and the discussion treats it as an original and widely used tool. Others (Linnarsson, Sandberg, Wahren-Herlenius in her response) put it behind other candidates because it is a method with little clinical translation so far, and ask why a tool counts under Physiology or Medicine.

B032 (BCR-ABL): Linnarsson keeps it as an alternative for its mature, decades-long survival data. El Manira, Sandberg and Wahren-Herlenius each respond that it applies earlier oncogene and kinase biology credited to others, and so reads as an application more than a distinct discovery.

B048 (UPR) and B045 (SMN2 antisense): members regard both as original mechanisms with coherent pairs. The dispute is whether the UPR link to medical practice is too indirect (Sandberg ranks it sixth, Svenningsson sees it as the stronger fundamental discovery than B044) and whether B045 is first-tier or early (Perlmann and El Manira, with Linnarsson saying less urgency this year).
attribution_disputes: B033: whether Mojsov's identification and synthesis of the active GLP-1(7-36) peptide can be credited over or alongside Habener and colleagues, who are outside the credited names. Wahren-Herlenius holds her own judgement that Mojsov is distinct enough to credit, and Svenningsson holds the same judgement with some uncertainty. No member can resolve the question from the supplied text, and several rely on memory of priority histories.

B033: whether Knudsen should displace one of the basic-science trio, or be omitted as a recorded choice. El Manira would revisit Knudsen only if Mojsov's priority cannot be defended. Perlmann, Sandberg and Wahren-Herlenius would not give Knudsen the third slot in place of Mojsov, or would want any such substitution made explicitly and not quietly.

B026: the shortlist lists June, Sadelain and Rosenberg. Members who comment would credit only June and Sadelain, and several note that Eshhar's chimeric receptor concept is outside the credited names and makes any configuration from this list incomplete.

B007: six credited names against a three-person cap, so Bamberg, Boyden and Miesenböck (or whichever three are cut) would be excluded. El Manira and Svenningsson say this exclusion cannot be defended on priority alone.

B051: Feldmann and Maini are a clean pair, but members note TNF biology and antibody engineering by others (for example Cerami, Vilcek, Kollias) lie outside the credited names. Wahren-Herlenius asks for the allocation to be checked against earlier TNF work.
maturity_disputes: No member disputes the maturity of B033. All six say outcome trials are in and the mechanism is understood.

B045: whether long-term evidence is long enough for 2026, given that Perlmann and El Manira describe it as strong but somewhat early, and that Linnarsson sees a generality of the platform still being demonstrated.
B007: whether clinical translation, which members describe as limited to early retinal work, matters for a method prize, or whether the impact on experimental neuroscience suffices.

B051 and B032: both are mature, and the disagreement concerns whether maturity here means a newer achievement or an older, already-absorbed one. Wahren-Herlenius notes it is a less recent, more incremental change than CAR-T.
conflict_or_recusal_flags: Svenningsson (chair) discloses about twenty co-authored works with fellow member Perlmann on dopamine neuron topics and a postdoctoral period with Paul Greengard. Neither involves a credited name on B033, B026 or B007.

Perlmann discloses the same co-authorship with Svenningsson, one 2009 paper with El Manira, and a co-authorship with Ronald Evans, who is not credited on any shortlisted ballot. None concerns a shortlisted candidate.

Wahren-Herlenius notes that B051 (TNF blockade) lies in her clinical field of rheumatology and that she has no documented link to Feldmann or Maini. She says she will check the credited names against her co-authorship record before voting if an autoimmunity candidate is taken up.

El Manira, Linnarsson and Sandberg each report no specific conflict with a shortlisted candidate. Their listed co-authorships (Grillner, Ernfors, Perlmann; Sandberg and spatial transcriptomics; Linnarsson, Frisén, Burge) do not involve credited names. Shared KI affiliation is not treated as a conflict.
questions_for_round2: Is the B033 achievement the physiology of GLP-1 or the drug development that made it a medicine? If it is both, which of the three slots would Knudsen take, and what would the citation then say?

Can the Mojsov versus Habener priority on the active GLP-1(7-36) peptide be settled from the nomination evidence and the record, and if it cannot, does Mojsov stay in the trio, and on what stated basis?

If B026 is the main alternative, can June and Sadelain be credited with a citation that is honest about Eshhar's chimeric receptor concept and about Rosenberg's separate adoptive cell therapy line, or does that gap make the configuration unfit for 2026?

Is a two-part prize (B033 with a second achievement) acceptable if the three-person cap would cut the GLP-1 part to fewer than three names, and would any member support that cost? Which second candidate would be proposed?

If GLP-1 does not hold, which alternative does each member prefer from B026, B007, B051, B032 and B048, and why? Members should address the attribution gap that each carries (Eshhar for B026, six credited names for B007, earlier TNF biology for B051, earlier oncogene work for B032, indirect clinical link for B048).
summary.chair_observation: The six round-1 files agree on B033 as the sole preferred part and on the Drucker, Holst and Mojsov trio. The remaining uncertainty is about credit, namely Mojsov against Habener and Knudsen against the three-person cap, and not about the science or the maturity of the work. The alternatives are spread across B026, B007, B051, B032 and B048, and only B026 appears on all six lists, so round 2 has little shared ground on a second part. No member has recorded a conflict that requires recusal, and several members rely on recalled priority histories that the files do not verify.
